current_example.problem:
Solve the following equation for the variable $x\mathbin{:}$

$$
\dfrac{3x-2y}{3}=\dfrac{1+2y}{4}
$$
current_example.worked_solution:
We need to isolate the variable $x.$ First, we cross-multiply:

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{3x-2y}{3} & =\frac{1+2y}{4} \\ 4\cdot (3x-2y) & =3\cdot (1+2y) \\ 12x-8y & =3+6y\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we add $8y$ to both sides of the equation:

$$
\begin{aligned}12x-8y & =3+6y \\ 12x-8y+8y & =3+6y+8y \\ 12x & =3+14y\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we divide both sides of the equation by $12\mathbin{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}12x & =3+14y \\ \frac{12x}{12} & =\frac{3+14y}{12} \\ \frac{\cancel{12}x}{\cancel{12}} & =\frac{3+14y}{12} \\ x & =\frac{3+14y}{12}\end{aligned}
$$
